analyst_view.overall: Bottom against top at the Alfonso Murube on Monday night: Ceuta are last with 5 points, six straight defeats, the fewest goals (10) and the most conceded (32), and this is Sergio Lobera's home debut after a 2-0 loss at Tenerife; the club is handing season-ticket holders free tickets to fill the ground, and Lobera calls beating the leader at home the best possible turning point. Almería lead with 32 points (26 scored, 11 conceded) and get Marcos Luna back from a ban and Dzodic and Cipenga back from international duty, but captain Jorge Pulido dropped out on Sunday with ankle discomfort, joining Rodrigo Ely and Melamed (Melamed is in the numbers, Pulido is not). Sevikyan is in Ceuta's probable XI; Lobera named no absentees. Referee Eder Mallo Fernández (5.5 cards a game, near the average) is already counted.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.2 goals, with Ceuta's share helped by last season's 3-2 home win (+7.5% head-to-head from two meetings) and Melamed's absence taking about 6% off Almería. On Sunday morning I leaned slightly lower because Ceuta create so little, but Almería have now lost centre-back and captain Jorge Pulido, a starter the numbers don't know about, which gives Ceuta's weak attack a little more hope. The two balance, so I move back to 3.2.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.8 corners, 6.1 of them Ceuta's, already including their recent run of corners (+11% momentum, 44 in six). Lobera's possession game with high full-backs fits that pattern and García Pimienta expects a hard game rather than sitting back; Pulido's absence changes who heads crosses away, not how many corners come, so I stay at 9.8.

cards.text: The numbers say 6.1 cards, already counting Ceuta's heavy recent booking (+12% momentum) and referee Eder Mallo Fernández, whose 5.5 cards a game is close to the league average (+2.6%). A desperate home side in front of a full ground may foul to stop Almería's counters, but that is the pattern the numbers already see, so I stay at 6.1.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.4 shots, with Ceuta's recent volume adding 30% to their side and Almería's quieter attacking run taking about 7% off theirs. Lobera's side keeps the ball and shoots from range while Almería need few chances; a reshuffled Almería back line without Pulido may let Ceuta shoot a touch more, but that is within what the numbers already give them, so 31.4.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.3 shots on target. Ceuta hit the target only twice at Tenerife despite most of the ball, which kept me slightly lower this morning, but Almería now line up without Pulido at the back, which should make clean shots a little easier for Ceuta. Those offset, so I stay at 10.3; Almería's own accuracy is already in the numbers.
